warnings: DOOR AND WINDOW MARKS ARE NOT LISTED FROM THIS SHEET, for the same reason as A-04: the ป/น glyphs are ~10 px tall on this scan and A-14/A-15 carry the authoritative schedule. This plan is the denser of the two - the upper floor has windows on all four sides - so guessing here would produce more phantom marks, not fewer.

THE ROOM NUMBERED ห้องน้ำ 1 IS ON THIS FLOOR AND SO IS AN UNNUMBERED ห้องน้ำ; ห้องน้ำ 3 IS DOWNSTAIRS ON A-04. That makes the unnumbered one ห้องน้ำ 2 by elimination, and A-11/A-12/A-13 being titled แบบขยายห้องน้ำ 1 / 2 / 3 confirms the set has exactly three. The id is recorded as ห้องน้ำ_2 with the reasoning on the element and a flag, rather than left as a duplicate ห้องน้ำ that would collide under §0.3.

LEVELS ARE CONSISTENT AND MEANINGFUL: the floor slab is +4.00, both bathrooms drop 50 mm to +3.95, and the balcony drops 100 mm to +3.90 - the standard wet-area and outdoor steps. Floor-to-floor from the +0.60 living level is 3.40 m.

GRID CHAINS MATCH THE MASTER: 3.50/2.20/3.00 = 8.70 and 2.00/0.80/4.00/3.00/1.60 = 11.40, plus 1.00 eave projections beyond ง' and ก. Sub-chains printed only here (0.90/0.80, 0.85/1.20, 0.80/0.50/0.85, 1.10/1.60, 0.40/0.75, 0.20/0.40, 1.00/0.75) locate walls and openings, not structure; none was used to add a grid line.

The upper floor footprint is smaller than the ground floor - it stops at ง and does not extend over the kitchen/washing wing, which is why the roof plan on the same sheet shows a stepped hip. That agrees with S-02, where the ง'-to-ง'' strip is roof framing rather than a floor.
This file covers the LEFT view only. The right view (แปลนหลังคา) is a separate file per §3.

OPENING VOCABULARY RESOLVED ON A-14/A-15 (หน้า15, หน้า16). This file records no ป/น marks because the glyphs are unreadable at this scan's resolution. The schedules give the full closed list - eight door types ป1-ป8 and nine window types น1-น9, seventeen marks - so any later pass adding positions to this sheet has a fixed vocabulary to match against and cannot invent a mark. What is still missing is only WHICH type sits in WHICH opening on this drawing.
